href: data_wrangling_prac_s.qmd text: "Practice Slides" --- ## R - Language {background-image="images/r_rstudio.png" background-size="contain" background-opacity="0.4"} - Developed in the early 1990s\ -Ross Ihaka and Robert Gentleman at the University of Auckland, New Zealand\ - A powerful language for statistical computing and graphics\ - Widely used by statisticians, data scientists, and researchers\ - RStudio: User Interface ![](images/r_rstudio.png){.absolute left="500" top="02" width="300"} ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Why Use R - Extensive libraries for data analysis and visualization\ - Active community support\ - Cross-platform compatibility (Windows, MacOS, Linux)\ - Integration with Python and C++\ - Free and open-source ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Key Features of R - Comprehensive statistical analysis tools\ - Advanced graphics capabilities with `ggplot2`\ - Rich ecosystem of packages (`dplyr`, `tidyr`)\ - Interactive and reproducible research with RMarkdown or Quarto ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## R vs Python ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ### R - Designed for statistical analysis and visualization\ - Rich ecosystem: `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `caret`\ - Preferred in academia and research\ ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Python - General-purpose language\ - Strong in data science and ML: `pandas`, `scikit-learn`, `TensorFlow`\ - Versatile for web, automation, and more\ ::: ::::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Installation of R and RStudio - R: [CRAN Windows](https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/base/)\ - R: [CRAN MacOS](https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/base/R-4.6.0-arm64.pkg)\ - RStudio: [RStudio Desktop - Posit](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## R 4.4.1 {background-image="images/r_base_gui_4.6.jpg" background-size="contain" background-opacity="0.9"} ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## RStudio Interface {background-image="images/r_environment.jpg" background-size="contain" background-opacity="0.9"} ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Project - Centralized Management\ - Consistent Environment\ - Version Control Integration\ - Quicker Setup ## Project: why not `setwd()`? - A **Project** (`.Rproj`) makes its own folder the working directory every time you open it - Paths are then **relative to the project**: `read_csv("data/ncd_survey.csv")` works on any computer - `setwd("C:/Users/Asha/Desktop")` only works on one machine, and breaks when you share the script - Keep raw data in `data/`, write all steps in a **script** (not only the console), and never overwrite the raw file ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Global options {background-image="images/global_options.jpg" background-size="contain" background-opacity="0.9"} ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## New File — Core R Authoring - **R Script** — plain R code file for scripts and functions - **R Notebook** — interactive notebook with code, output, and narrative - **R Markdown** — reproducible reports combining R and text - **Quarto Document** — modern multi-language document format for reports - **Quarto Presentation** — slide decks built from Quarto content ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## New File — Documentation & Static Content - **R HTML** — HTML pages generated from R code and content - **R Documentation** — help files for packages and functions - **Text File** — plain text for notes, configs, or simple drafts ::: {when-level="moderate"} ## New File — Other Languages & Tools {.smaller} - **Python Script** — Python code file for reticulate and Python work - **C++ File** — C++ source for Rcpp or performance-critical code - **SQL Script** — SQL queries and database interactions - **Stan File** — Stan model code for Bayesian modeling - **D3 Script** — D3 JavaScript visualizations - **R Sweave** — LaTeX+R documents for PDF reporting - **Shiny Web App** — interactive apps built with Shiny - **Plumber API** — R APIs exposed as web services ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Variables and Data Types {.smaller} - **Numeric** — numbers such as `3.14`, `42` - **Integer** — whole numbers with `L` suffix, e.g. `5L` - **Character** — text values like `"data"` - **Logical** — `TRUE` or `FALSE` - **Factor** — categorical values with levels - **Complex** — numbers with imaginary parts like `1 + 2i` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} x <- 5 # numeric name <- "Alice" # character flag <- TRUE # logical colors <- factor(c("red", "blue", "green")) ``` ::: - Variables store values in memory and can be reused later - R is dynamically typed: type depends on the stored value ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Vectors and Sequences - Create ordered collections with `c()` and sequences with `seq()` - Useful for numeric data, indexes, and repeated values ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ages <- c(23, 35, 28) seq(1, 100, 3) seq(1, 2, length.out = 10) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Factors and Categorical Variables - Store categories or groups with fixed levels - Important for statistical modeling and reporting - Use `factor()` to make discrete labels or ordered categories ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} gender <- factor(c("Male", "Female", "Male", "Female"), levels = c("Male", "Female")) physical_activity <- factor(sample(c(1, 2), 10, replace = TRUE), levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Yes", "No")) ``` ::: ## Factor levels and the reference level ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} res <- factor(c("Urban", "Rural", "Urban")) levels(res) # sorted alphabetically by default: "Rural" "Urban" ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] "Rural" "Urban" ``` ::: ::: - Unless you set `levels =` yourself, R sorts levels **alphabetically**; the **first level is the reference** in models - Choose it deliberately: `factor(x, levels = c("Urban", "Rural"))` - Text in quotes is a **character**, not a number: `mean(c("45", "52"))` fails. Convert with `as.numeric()` ## Missing values spread ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} wt <- c(60, 72, NA, 58) mean(wt) # NA: one unknown value makes the mean unknown ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] NA ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} mean(wt, na.rm = TRUE) # drop the missing value for this calculation (and report it) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 63.33333 ``` ::: ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Lists and Matrices {.smaller} ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Lists - Store mixed types in one object - Can contain vectors, data frames, functions, or other lists - Good for nested results and complex outputs ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} my_list <- list(name = "Alice", score = 95, data = c(1, 2, 3)) ``` ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ### Matrices - Two-dimensional arrays with a single data type - Ideal for numeric calculations, matrices, and linear algebra - Built from vectors using `matrix()`, `cbind()`, or `rbind()` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m <- matrix(1:9, nrow = 3) ``` ::: ::: ::::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Data Structures {.smaller} - Data frames are the most common table structure in R - They combine columns of equal length and can contain different types - Lists and matrices are also important foundational structures ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} my_data <- data.frame( ID = 1:5, Name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie", "David", "Eva"), Age = sample(20:50, 5, replace = TRUE) ) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Functions and Control Flow - Functions are reusable blocks of code created with `function()` - Control flow uses `if`, `else`, `for`, `while` and `repeat` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} add <- function(a, b) { result <- a + b return(result) } if (add(2, 3) > 4) { print("Yes, it is greater than 4") } ``` ::: - Functions help organize logic and avoid repetition - Control flow enables conditional decisions and loops ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Packages - Collections of functions, data, and compiled code\ - Installation: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} install.packages(c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "readxl", "gtsummary", "ggstatsplot", "flextable", "pacman")) ``` ::: ------------------------------------------------------------------------ ## Installation {.smaller} - Install a single package: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} install.packages("dplyr") ``` ::: - Install several packages: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} install.packages(c("tidyverse", "ggplot2", "readxl")) ``` ::: - Use `pacman` to install and load packages automatically: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} if (!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman") pacman::p_load(tidyverse, ggplot2, readxl, gtsummary, ggstatsplot, flextable) ``` ::: - `pacman::p_load()` installs missing packages and loads them in one command. ## 🔧 Practise in R {.smaller} Download the lab **[Your first script](../labs/basic/b1_first_script.R)** and the data ([ncd_survey.csv](../data/ncd_survey.csv)). Fill in the blanks (`___`); the comments say what each step should do. 🗺️ Then play the game world **[Your First Script](../../dungeons/dungeons/b1_first_script.html)** in *Dungeons & Dataframes*. ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="gs1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="rkhcw5.v9056p" data-show="SXQgcmV0dXJucyBOQQ==" data-explain="QSBtaXNzaW5nIHZhbHVlIG1ha2VzIHRoZSBtZWFuIHVua25vd24sIHNvIFIgcmV0dXJucyBO QS4gYG1lYW4oeCwgbmEucm0gPSBUUlVFKWAgbGVhdmVzIHRoZSBtaXNzaW5nIHZhbHVlIG91 dCBhbmQgZ2l2ZXMgNi4="} You type `x <- c(4, 8, NA)` and then `mean(x)`. What does R return? - It returns NA - It returns 6 - It returns 4 - It stops with an error ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="gs2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="rkhq4v.v90jo3" data-show="UGF0aHMgc3RhcnQgYXQgdGhlIHByb2plY3QgZm9sZGVyLCBzbyBpdCBydW5zIGFueXdoZXJl " data-explain="QSBwcm9qZWN0IHNldHMgdGhlIHdvcmtpbmcgZGlyZWN0b3J5IHRvIGl0cyBvd24gZm9sZGVy LCBzbyByZWxhdGl2ZSBwYXRocyBzdWNoIGFzIGRhdGEvbmNkX3N1cnZleS5jc3Ygd29yayBv biBhbnkgY29tcHV0ZXIu"} Why does the deck recommend an RStudio Project rather than `setwd()`? - setwd() is slower when the dataset loaded is large - Paths start at the project folder, so it runs anywhere - Projects install every package that the script needs to run - setwd() works on Windows, but it fails on macOS or Linux ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="gs3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="rki3dl.v90y5h" data-show="RmVtYWxlLCB0aGUgZmlyc3QgbGV2ZWwgaW4gYWxwaGFiZXRpY2FsIG9yZGVy" data-explain="UiBvcmRlcnMgZmFjdG9yIGxldmVscyBhbHBoYWJldGljYWxseSB1bmxlc3MgdG9sZCBvdGhl cndpc2UsIGFuZCB0aGUgZmlyc3QgbGV2ZWwgaXMgdGhlIHJlZmVyZW5jZS4gYHJlbGV2ZWwo KWAgb3IgYGZhY3RvcihsZXZlbHMgPSApYCBjaGFuZ2VzIGl0Lg=="} `sex` is a factor with the levels Female and Male. Which level is the reference in a model, by default? - The level with more people in the data - Male, the last level of the factor - Female, the first level in alphabetical order - None: R estimates a coefficient for every level ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="gs4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="rkigmb.v91cmv" data-show="QSBkYXRhIGZyYW1l" data-explain="QSBkYXRhIGZyYW1lIGlzIGEgbGlzdCBvZiBlcXVhbC1sZW5ndGggY29sdW1ucyB0aGF0IG1h eSBoYXZlIGRpZmZlcmVudCB0eXBlczsgYSBtYXRyaXggaG9sZHMgb25lIHR5cGUgb25seS4="} Which object holds several columns of different types, one row per patient? - A numeric vector - A matrix of numbers - A single factor - A data frame ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="gs5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="rkitux.v91r45" data-show="RG93bmxvYWRzIHRoZSBwYWNrYWdlIHRvIHlvdXIgY29tcHV0ZXIsIG9uY2U=" data-explain="aW5zdGFsbC5wYWNrYWdlcygpIGRvd25sb2FkcyBhbmQgaW5zdGFsbHMgYSBwYWNrYWdlIG9u Y2UgcGVyIGNvbXB1dGVyOyBsaWJyYXJ5KCkgbG9hZHMgYW4gaW5zdGFsbGVkIHBhY2thZ2Ug aW50byBlYWNoIG5ldyBzZXNzaW9uLg=="} What does `install.packages("dplyr")` do that `library(dplyr)` does not? - Downloads the package to your computer, once - Loads the package into the current R session only - Updates R itself to the newest release - Checks the package for errors before use ::: ## Score {.smaller} **Your score: ** (first attempt counts) ```{=html} ```

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
